title: Customising Your Workspace 🎛️
description: Save layouts, tweak preferences, and set up hotkeys for speed.

slides.title: Layouts – Your Personal Cockpit ✈️
slides.content:
# Save Your Perfect Setup

You’ve learned to move panels. Now save that arrangement as a **custom layout**:

1. Arrange panels exactly how you like.
2. Go to **Window → Save Layout**.
3. Name it (e.g., "My Game Dev Mode").

Your layout appears under **Window → Layout** for quick switching. You can also export/import layouts to share with a team.

*Analogy:* It’s like saving different tool benches – one for modelling, one for scripting, one for debugging.

quizData.question: To save your current panel arrangement, go to Window → _____ Layout.
quizData.explanation: Use Window → Save Layout to store your custom arrangement for later use.

slides.title: Editor Preferences ⚙️
slides.content:
## Make the Editor Yours

Go to **Edit → Editor Preferences** to tweak:

* **Appearance** – change UI colours, font size.
* **Viewport** – mouse sensitivity, invert axis.
* **Loading & Saving** – auto‑save frequency.
* **Source Control** – connect to Git/Perforce.
* **Experimental** – new features (use with caution).

Spend a few minutes browsing – you’ll find quality‑of‑life settings you didn’t know you needed.

slides.title: Project Settings vs Editor Preferences 🆚
slides.content:
## Don’t Confuse Them!

* **Editor Preferences** – affect *your* editor instance only (applies to all projects).
* **Project Settings** – saved inside the project, shared with your team.

Example: Want bigger viewport text for yourself? Editor Preferences. Want to set the game’s default resolution? Project Settings.

quizData.question: Which settings are stored per‑project and shared with teammates?
quizData.explanation: Project Settings are saved in the project’s Config folder and affect everyone opening the project.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Enable Auto‑Save

In Editor Preferences, under **Loading & Saving**, enable **Auto‑Save**. Set the interval to 5 minutes. This saves a copy of your work regularly – a lifesaver during crashes.
